items.title: The battery runs down overnight while the console is asleep
summary: Reported on 28 October 2026: a 4-inch E32R40T build on 5.12.4, with a 3000 mAh pack and Wi-Fi set up, went from full to about 10% overnight with the screen dark.
Asleep, Braino turns the backlight off and puts the panel to sleep. The processor keeps running and Wi-Fi stays connected.
Next: measure the current drawn while asleep, then cut it.

images.alt: The Braino! lock screen, shown on waking, with the battery badge at the top right

items.title: Washed-out colours on the dual-USB CYD (CYD2USB)
summary: The dual-USB 2.8-inch CYD has ST7789 glass. Today it runs the inverted-panel image, which drives it as an ILI9341: it works, and the colours come out washed out.
A new board profile drives it as an ST7789. The build is on the Experimental page, waiting for the person who reported it to try it on their board.

images.alt: GPIO table for the ESP32-2432S028 with ST7789 glass: display, touch, audio, RGB LED, SD card and BOOT key pins

items.title: NumberNest
summary: Five numbers in five circles. One of them is the sum of two of the others, or in Multiply their product: tap it. Five answers fill a nest, and the nest is the last group to solve.
Five levels for adding and five for multiplying, saved per player. Six right first time in a row earns the next level.

items.title: Sign ABC
summary: The American Sign Language hand alphabet, A to Z, as a course. Seven lessons of four letters: each shows its new hands one at a time, beside the letter, then asks six questions, a hand for a letter and a letter for a hand.
J and Z are signed by moving the hand, so they carry the movement as an arrow. Practice quizzes every letter learnt so far, and the letters a player misses come back sooner.
Hand artwork from WPClipart's public-domain set.

images.alt: Sign ABC's lesson list: A to D and E to H done, I to L next, the rest locked, and Practice

items.title: Attaky Core
summary: An ESP32-S3 board with a 2.0-inch 240x320 ST7789 panel and capacitive touch. The port adds the D-pad to the launcher and typing from the clip-on keyboard in every text field.
Written from the published pin map, and not yet run on a device.

images.alt: GPIO table for the Attaky Core: touch, SD card, display, audio, module check and BOOT key pins
